issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Rideable.messageOnRide: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() that returns a String (used as r.messageOnRide() in Main and described in the UML and text). The solution repository defines the interface method as messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it in Pig and Seal with an int parameter. This discrepancy prevents code written against the template/problem (which calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments) from compiling against the solution types and confuses students about which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix preserving the problem statement and template: change the solution's Rideable interface to declare String messageOnRide() (no parameters), and update Pig and Seal implementations to provide messageOnRide() that return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Alternatively, if the intent is to include a speed parameter, update the problem statement, the UML, and the template Main usage to call messageOnRide(int speed) and document the parameter, ensuring all artifacts use the same signature.

issues.description: The concept is the Rideable.messageOnRide operation (the action of riding an animal and returning a message). The problem statement / UML (problem_statement.md) and the example usage in the template Main.java expect a no-argument method Rideable.messageOnRide() returning String and call r.messageOnRide() with no parameters. However, the solution repository defines the interface as Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementations Seal.messageOnRide(int) and Pig.messageOnRide(int). This is an identifier/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation: the problem and template require messageOnRide() (no args) while the solution defines messageOnRide(int). Students will be unsure which signature to implement and how to call it; following one artifact leads to compile errors or incorrect implementations against the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature the same across all artifacts. Recommended: change the solution to match the problem/template by updating Rideable to declare String messageOnRide() (no parameters) and update Seal and Pig implementations to implement messageOnRide() returning the required string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an integer speed parameter is desired pedagogically, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main.java to require messageOnRide(int speed) (and update the example usages and textual instructions accordingly). Option A (no-arg messageOnRide()) is recommended to align with the current exercise description and template usage.
